acceptance_note: The input is the set of rows the owner's written policy accepted. No analyst, human, or supervisor reviewed any row. The design brief's phrase 'analyst-accepted matches' is not yet satisfied by a person, and no artifact here describes it as such.

direction_application.note: every offered direction reaches exactly one outcome; none is dropped

direction_application_after_ruling.interpretation: the ruling confirms the measurement that prompted it: of the 163 previously deferred cases, 154 were one carriageway split at junctions and only 9 had genuinely divergent bearings. Those 9 still defer, and the 61 unresolved directions are unchanged because no member edge lies within the tolerance at all.

explicit_non_claims: no demand artifact has been produced; this record covers input preparation only
reconstructed routes would be count-constrained candidates, never observed origin-destination travel
no calibration, comparison, or simulation was performed
MAN-09 remains planned and Gate D remains foundation_only
gate: Gate-D step 5 (demand reconstruction), input preparation only

inputs.reproduction_check: the v1.1 run was re-executed from the accepted snapshots and reproduced 131 accepted / 165 awaiting manual review / 9 no suitable candidate, matching the Phase 3/4 record exactly

not_yet_done.reason: route pool generation and routeSampler execution are the next step; the direction binding they depend on is now settled at 241 of 311 site-directions.
not_yet_done.tooling_verified_available: SUMO 1.27.1 with tools/routeSampler.py and tools/randomTrips.py present; dfrouter deliberately not used because SUMO documentation warns it can produce implausible routes in highly meshed city networks

owner_ruling.collinearity_bound: the already-approved 45 degree direction tolerance, applied pairwise between the compatible edges. No second threshold was introduced.
owner_ruling.decision: collinear same-direction fragments of one road group count as a single binding target
owner_ruling.lineage: the whole collapsed fragment set and the measured pairwise spread are recorded on every collinear binding, so edge-level lineage survives the collapse
owner_ruling.no_distance_available: if no distance to the count point is available the fragment carrying the count cannot be identified, so the direction still defers rather than binding to an arbitrary fragment
owner_ruling.rationale_recorded: the 'several compatible edges' rule was written for the two opposing carriageways; SUMO splits one carriageway at every junction, so fragments of the same road were being deferred as if they were opposing directions
owner_ruling.which_fragment_receives_the_count: the fragment nearest the count point. A point count constrains the edge the count point physically sits on; binding it to every fragment would assert the same flow across intervening junctions.

substantive_finding_for_the_owner.consequence: As first measured, only 87 of 311 site-directions bound, across 53 of the 131 accepted sites, which would have left route sampling severely under-constrained. This finding was put to the owner rather than engineered around, and the ruling recorded under owner_ruling resolved it.
substantive_finding_for_the_owner.interpretation: The approved rule 'if both directed edges remain plausible, keep both and require analyst confirmation' was written for the two opposing carriageways of one road. In practice it fires most often because SUMO splits a single carriageway at every junction, so several fragments of the same road run within a couple of degrees of each other and all satisfy the 45 degree tolerance. That is a grouping artifact rather than genuine directional ambiguity.
substantive_finding_for_the_owner.measurement_correction: an earlier pass computed the spread as max(bearing) - min(bearing), which is wrong for circular data and reported a spurious maximum of 359.50 degrees for edges lying either side of north. The figures above use the maximum pairwise circular difference and give a true maximum of 76.03 degrees.
substantive_finding_for_the_owner.not_decided_here: Nothing was decided by this agent. The three options were put to the owner, who chose the first on 25 July 2026; see owner_ruling and direction_application_after_ruling for the decision and its measured effect.
options_for_the_owner: treat collinear same-direction fragments of one road group as a single binding target, so the count binds once to that road rather than deferring
keep the current rule and accept the reduced coverage, recording it as a limitation
raise the confirmation rule's threshold so it fires only when compatible bearings genuinely diverge
substantive_finding_for_the_owner.resolution: owner chose option 1: collinear same-direction fragments count as one binding target. 154 of the 163 deferred cases were one carriageway split at junctions; the remaining 9 had genuinely divergent bearings and still defer.
substantive_finding_for_the_owner.summary: the 'several compatible edges' rule fires mostly on collinear fragments of one carriageway, not on opposing directions

why_direction_is_applied_here: The approved policy sequences it this way: reference matching first identifies an undirected road group, and the raw count's direction is applied afterwards to the underlying directed SUMO edges. Policy v1.1 accordingly leaves bearing_degrees unset, so this is the first stage at which direction exists.
